status_note: Stand-in until the platform's rules engine is connected (design 7.4: 'the same verdicts Mr. AI shows'). Built from the UP Startup Atlas scheme research (raw/L5_policy/schemes.csv), whose facts were checked on 1 October 2026 against the sources given; a review on 27-28 October 2026 corrected the schemes that carry a changed_on date (the change_note says what changed and why). The engine knows only public facts about a company, so most verdicts are 'check required' with the missing facts listed; it never says 'eligible' for a scheme with conditions it cannot see, and an unknown fact never makes a rule fire. A 'closed' verdict must carry valid_until: after that date it is shown as 'check required' until someone re-checks the scheme. Verdicts from this file are shown in the Admin pages and are never used in a message until confirmed_by is filled in or the platform endpoint replaces them.

verdicts.eligible: Every condition is met by facts we hold.
verdicts.check_required: No condition fails on the facts we hold, but some can only be checked with the founder.
verdicts.not_eligible: A condition fails on a fact we hold.
verdicts.closed: The scheme is not taking applications (until valid_until, after which it must be re-checked).

schemes.name: DPIIT startup recognition
schemes.benefit: The gateway to Startup India benefits: the tax holiday, the seed fund, credit guarantees, government procurement relaxations and lower patent fees.

rules.reason: A public limited company is not among the entities the 2026 framework recognises (private limited companies, LLPs, registered partnerships and cooperative societies).
Older than 20 years, the limit even for deep-tech startups.

Recognition is open to a private limited company, an LLP, a registered partnership or a cooperative society. Whether this company counts as a private limited company (a Section 8 company, a foreign company's subsidiary or a government company may or may not be one) must be checked.
Older than 10 years, so it qualifies only as a deep-tech startup (up to 20 years and ₹300 crore turnover).

default.reason: The type of entity and its age qualify. Recognition also needs an innovative or scalable business and turnover of at most ₹200 crore in every year since incorporation.

schemes.law: DPIIT notification of 4 February 2026 (reported as G.S.R. 108(E)), replacing G.S.R. 127(E) of 19 February 2019
schemes.verified_against: PIB release of 5 February 2026 and the definition reproduced in the UP Startup Policy 2026 annex (entity list, 10/20 years, ₹200/300 crore)
schemes.change_note: Every type other than PTC, OPC and LLP was 'not eligible'. The definition names a 'private limited company' with no ownership condition, so a foreign company's private subsidiary (FTC) qualifies, and the CIN cannot tell whether a Section 8 company (NPL) is private. Only public companies (PLC) stay 'not eligible'; the others are 'check required'.

schemes.name: Startup tax holiday (Income-tax Act 2025 s.140, formerly 80-IAC)
schemes.benefit: 100% of profits tax-free for any three consecutive years out of the first ten.

rules.reason: The deduction needs a certificate from the Inter-Ministerial Board, which is given only to DPIIT-recognised startups, and a public company cannot be recognised.
Open to a company or an LLP that holds DPIIT recognition and the Inter-Ministerial Board's certificate; whether this type of company can be recognised must be checked first.

default.reason: Incorporated within the window (1 April 2016 to 31 March 2030). It needs DPIIT recognition first, then a certificate from the Inter-Ministerial Board, and turnover of at most ₹100 crore in the year claimed.

schemes.law: Income-tax Act 2025 s.140 (an 'eligible start-up' is a company or an LLP, s.140(16)(b))
schemes.verified_against: Income-tax Bill 2025 as passed, s.140(1)-(3) and (16)
schemes.change_note: The statute says 'a company or a limited liability partnership', not 'a private limited company'. Public companies stay 'not eligible' because they cannot get DPIIT recognition, which the Board's certificate needs; other company types are now 'check required'.

schemes.name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme
schemes.benefit: Up to ₹20 lakh grant for a proof of concept and up to ₹50 lakh as debt or convertibles, through selected incubators.

rules.reason: Incorporated more than two years ago; the scheme takes startups incorporated not more than two years before they apply.

default.reason: Startups apply through the incubators selected under the scheme, on seedfund.startupindia.gov.in. Whether a call for startups is open must be checked there: a last date of 31 May 2026 was reported by a third-party site but not confirmed from an official notice, and the Government's answer in Parliament on 17 March 2026 describes the scheme as running. The startup must be DPIIT-recognised and incorporated not more than two years before it applies.

schemes.law: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme guidelines (from 1 April 2021), eligibility criterion 1
schemes.verified_against: Scheme guidelines (eligibility: DPIIT-recognised, incorporated not more than 2 years ago at the time of application); PIB release of 17 March 2026
schemes.change_note: Was 'closed' (applications closed on 31 May 2026), citing a PIB release that does not say so; no official notice of a closure was found. Now 'check required', with the two-year age limit from the guidelines as the one fact-based 'not eligible'.

schemes.name: Startup in UP recognition (UP Startup Policy 2026)
schemes.benefit: The gateway to every UP startup incentive, and free incubation for two years at a recognised incubator.

rules.reason: Listed on the Startup in UP portal.

default.reason: Incorporated in UP. It also needs DPIIT recognition, registration on StartinUP and incubation at a StartinUP-recognised incubator (not needed from the scaling stage).

schemes.verified_against: UP Startup Policy 2026, cl.7A.1 and the note on incubation

schemes.name: UP sustenance allowance
schemes.benefit: ₹20,000 a month for two years (up to ₹4.8 lakh) until the prototype stage.

rules.reason: The allowance runs only until the prototype stage, and the portal lists this startup at a later stage ({stage}). The portal's stage is self-declared and may be out of date, so the current stage must be confirmed.
Listed on Startup in UP and incubated. It still needs DPIIT recognition and the incubator's recommendation.

default.reason: Needs DPIIT recognition, StartinUP registration and incubation at a StartinUP-recognised incubator, with its recommendation, before the prototype stage ends.

schemes.verified_against: UP Startup Policy 2026 cl.7A.2(i) ('till prototype stage') and the policy's own order of stages ('ideation, validation, prototyping, product development, market access and scale-up')
schemes.change_note: Startups at the 'validation' stage were 'not eligible', but the policy puts validation before prototyping, and the match was case-sensitive (the portal writes both 'validation' and 'Validation'). The stage is now compared without regard to case, validation counts as before the prototype, and a later stage gives 'check required' rather than 'not eligible' because the portal's stage is self-declared.

schemes.name: UP prototype grant
schemes.benefit: Up to ₹10 lakh for building a prototype (50% more for women-led startups, Purvanchal or Bundelkhand offices, and agri, circular or climate sectors).

rules.reason: Listed on Startup in UP and incubated. It still needs DPIIT recognition and the incubator's recommendation; software qualifies only if it is a standalone, technically advanced product.

default.reason: Needs DPIIT recognition, StartinUP registration and incubation at a StartinUP-recognised incubator, with its recommendation. Basic websites and simple apps do not qualify.

schemes.name: Udyam (MSME) registration
schemes.benefit: Free registration that brings 45-day payment protection from buyers, collateral-free loan guarantees (CGTMSE) and public-procurement benefits.

default.reason: Open to micro, small and medium enterprises (micro: investment up to ₹2.5 crore and turnover up to ₹10 crore). Registration is free and self-declared.

schemes.law: MSMED Act 2006; MSME classification revised from 1 April 2025
schemes.verified_against: PIB Budget 2025-26 release (limits raised 2.5 and 2 times)

schemes.name: PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (employer incentive)
schemes.benefit: Up to ₹3,000 a month for two years for each additional EPFO-registered employee kept for six months or more.

rules.reason: Only for jobs created up to 31 July 2027.

default.reason: Relevant once it hires: it must register with EPFO and add at least two employees (salary up to ₹1 lakh a month) for jobs created by 31 July 2027.

schemes.verified_against: PIB release of 25 July 2025 (jobs created 1 August 2025 to 31 July 2027; ₹3,000 a month; two more employees for employers under 50)
schemes.change_note: The 'closed' verdict now carries valid_until (three months after the scheme's end), after which it must be re-checked in case the scheme is extended.
